title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: params, roles, stop/logprobs, streaming & response formatting
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: bring Redwood's /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer to parity with OpenAI semantics for params, role handling, stop tokens, logprobs, streaming output formatting, and function/tool call shapes. This change unblocks customers using the OpenAI-compatible API surface and fixes inconsistencies observed in streaming message boundaries and stop/logprobs edge cases. Summary of changes: - Implement full `roles` normalization to accept system/user/assistant and preserve custom role strings when present. - Respect `stop` param semantics (single string, list of strings, prefix/suffix matches) and ensure streaming early termination triggers the same streamed delta + final chunk shape as OpenAI. - Surface `logprobs` and token-level `top_logprobs` fields in final non-streamed responses and attach best-effort partial logprobs during streaming when available from the runtime. - Standardize response formatting for structured output and tool/function calling: messages with function calls are emitted as assistant messages with `finish_reason` and structured `function_call` metadata. - Streaming stability: backpressure handling and chunk reassembly fixes in stream manager to avoid dropped tokens when client disconnects or slow consumers cause buffer buildup. - API surface: handler accepts OpenAI-style fields (model, messages, temperature, max_tokens, n, stop, logprobs, stream, functions, function_call) and maps them to internal request model with minimal semantic drift. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for roles/stop parsing and mapping - [x] Integration tests for streaming end-of-message boundaries - [x] E2E tests for function/tool call shaped responses - [x] Benchmarked decoding throughput impact (<2% median regression) - [x] Docs updated (openai_compat.md) Release plan: rollout as a staged feature flag for OpenAI-compat tenants, extra monitoring on streaming error rate and latency regressions. Links: implementation notes in Linear ENG-1245 and postmortem notes for previous streaming regressions (ENG-1310).
